class.name: TerrainGenerator3D
class.brief_description: Generates mountain ranges for a whole world by tectonic uplift against fluvial erosion, and writes them into the ground.
class.description: Simulates the large-scale landscape model of Cordonnier et al. 2016 ("Large Scale Terrain Generation from Tectonic Uplift and Fluvial Erosion"): rock rises at an uplift rate [code]U[/code], and rivers cut it by the stream power law [code]dh/dt = U - K A^m S[/code] (drainage area [code]A[/code], slope [code]S[/code]). Run towards equilibrium, the two make mountain ranges with connected, branching river valleys and the ridges between them, where uplift is high. The implicit solver of Braun and Willett 2013 makes every step stable at any [member time_step]. Closed basins are filled with sediment (Priority-Flood, Barnes et al. 2014), slopes are held under [member critical_slope], [member hillslope_diffusion] rounds hilltops, and drainage area is routed to all lower neighbours ([member flow_exponent]) so valleys do not follow the grid. Where the rock rises is the input: [member base_uplift] everywhere, a painted [member uplift_map] over the rectangle, Path3D [member ranges] (a band of [member range_width] around each curve), and an [member uplift_noise] that breaks them up. The grid is [member size] metres centred on the node, every [member cell_size] metres; a coarse cell size (8 to 32 m) is intended, since this is the world's large-scale shape. [method bake] (the inspector's Generate button) runs [method generate] then [method write_to_terrain], which samples the result bicubically onto the ground: a [code]Terrain3D[/code] node (called by name, never required; missing regions are created) or a [CollisionShape3D] with a [HeightMapShape3D], with an optional [member ground_mesh]. With a [member deformer], its brushes (rivers, roads, plots) are lifted before the write and applied again on the new ground. The simulation is single-threaded and runs in a fixed order, so the same settings and [member seed] give the same terrain on every machine. Only the starting roughness depends on the seed; it decides which drainage network forms. The result is not saved with the node (the ground keeps it). [method get_height], [method get_drainage_area] and [method get_sediment_depth] read it after [method generate].

method.name: bake
method.description: [method generate] then [method write_to_terrain]. Returns the number of vertices written.

method.name: generate
method.description: Runs [member steps] steps of uplift and erosion from a flat, slightly rough start. Returns [code]false[/code] if [member size] is empty.

method.name: get_drainage_area
method.description: Upstream drainage area at a world position, in square metres. Large values are rivers. NaN outside the rectangle or before [method generate].

method.name: get_drainage_image
method.description: Drainage area per grid node, [constant Image.FORMAT_RF], square metres.

method.name: get_grid_size
method.description: Grid nodes along X and Z of the last [method generate].

method.name: get_height
method.description: Generated ground height at a world position (bicubic between grid nodes, including [member height_offset]). NaN outside the rectangle or before [method generate].

method.name: get_height_image
method.description: Generated heights per grid node, [constant Image.FORMAT_RF], metres.

method.name: get_last_change
method.description: Largest height change in the last step, in metres. Small against [member uplift] times [member time_step] means the landscape is close to equilibrium.

method.name: get_last_generate_msec
method.description: Time the last [method generate] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_last_write_msec
method.description: Time the last [method write_to_terrain] took, in milliseconds.

method.name: get_sediment_depth
method.description: Thickness of sediment that filled closed basins during the simulation, in metres: flat valley floors and old lake beds.

method.name: get_sediment_image
method.description: Sediment thickness per grid node, [constant Image.FORMAT_RF], metres.

method.name: get_uplift_image
method.description: The uplift rate used per grid node, [constant Image.FORMAT_RF], millimetres per year.

method.name: get_world_rect
method.description: The world X and Z rectangle the generator covers ([code]position.y[/code] is Z).

method.name: has_result
method.description: Whether [method generate] has run since the node was created or [method clear_result].

method.name: write_to_terrain
method.description: Writes the generated heights into the ground's vertices inside the rectangle. Returns the number written.

members.member: Exponent [code]m[/code] of drainage area in the stream power law (slope exponent [code]n = 1[/code]). 0.4 to 0.6 is typical of real rivers; higher concentrates erosion in big valleys.
Uplift strength everywhere, 0 to 1, under the map and ranges. Low values give foothills between ranges.
Metres between grid nodes. Coarse on purpose: this stage shapes ranges and valleys, finer detail is added on top.
Steepest slope, in degrees, the rock holds along the flow direction; steeper ground collapses to it. 0 disables.
Optional [TerrainDeformer3D]. Its brushes are lifted before the write and applied again after it, and its terrain is used when [member terrain] is empty.
Stream power coefficient [code]K[/code]. Relief at equilibrium grows with [member uplift] / [member erodibility].

Drainage area is shared among all lower neighbours in proportion to slope to this power (multiple flow directions, Quinn et al. 1991, Freeman 1991). 0 routes all flow to the steepest neighbour (D8), which leaves straight 45 degree valleys.
The inspector's Generate button: runs [method bake].
A [MeshInstance3D] regenerated from a [HeightMapShape3D] ground after the write. The [member deformer]'s ground mesh is used when empty.
Added to every generated height.
Soil creep [code]k_d[/code] in square metres per year: rounds hilltops and softens ridges. 0 keeps sharp ridges.
Height of the seeded random roughness the simulation starts from, in metres.
When above 0, the relief is scaled so the highest point is this far above [member sea_level]. 0 keeps the simulated heights.
Edges of the rectangle held at [member sea_level] where water leaves: bits [constant OUTLET_NEGATIVE_X], [constant OUTLET_POSITIVE_X], [constant OUTLET_NEGATIVE_Z], [constant OUTLET_POSITIVE_Z].
Half width in metres of the uplift band around each Path3D in [member ranges]. A path's [code]width[/code] metadata overrides it, and its [code]uplift[/code] metadata sets its strength (default 1).
Path3D nodes along which mountain ranges rise.
Height of the outlets and of the flat start.
Seed of the starting roughness. Different seeds give different drainage networks on the same uplift.
Width (X) and depth (Z) in metres of the rectangle generated, centred on the node.
Time steps to simulate.
The ground to write: a [code]Terrain3D[/code] node or a [CollisionShape3D] with a [HeightMapShape3D].
Years per step. The solver is stable at any step; larger steps reach equilibrium sooner with less detail in the transient.
Uplift rate at full strength, in millimetres per year.
Uplift strength painted over the rectangle (red channel, 0 to 1).
Noise sampled at world X and Z that scales the uplift from the map and ranges down where it is low.
How far [member uplift_noise] can lower the uplift: where the noise is lowest the uplift is multiplied by [code]1 - strength[/code].
